report:
test_total does not fail. I ran the tests: 2 pass, 1 fails. test_total passes (it returns 359, as expected).

The failing test is test_half_cent_rounds_up: total([(1, 1010)], discount_percent=5) returns 959, the test expects 960.

Why: cart.total ends with int(subtotal * (1 - discount_percent / 100)). int() cuts off the fraction, it does not round. 1010 * 0.95 = 959.5, so int() gives 959. test_total passes only because 359.1 cuts down to 359, which is also the rounded value. This is the same bug as the TODO item "customers see totals one cent short".

I changed nothing. The fix is to round half up instead of truncating (for example with decimal.Decimal and ROUND_HALF_UP, since Python's round() rounds half to even and float math can drift). Say if you want me to make that change.
